summary: This is a well-scoped, additive Company -> Department -> Project dashboard drill-down plus a lightweight multi-project overview page. The security-critical piece (src/lib/company-scope.ts's requireCompanyScope) correctly verifies a real membership row before ever using a caller-supplied companyId as the VERIDIAN organizationId, which is what actually selects the per-org API key in veridian-client.ts's resolveApiKey() -- verified by reading that file directly since the file wasn't in the provided diff text. Cross-company isolation and the 403/401/400 paths are covered by real unit and route tests (company-scope.test.ts, dashboard/route.test.ts), not just claimed. The revenue pagination cap (MAX_INVOICE_PAGES) is disclosed to the caller via revenueTruncated rather than silently under-counting. No .github/workflows/** changes, no migrations/schema/sql/auth/permission/payment/billing/rls/security path matches, and the diff is purely additive (new files, devDependency additions, i18n strings, two new sidebar entries) -- consistent with the pre-assigned tier1 classification. UI code uses React's default escaping and drizzle's parameterized queries throughout; no injection or secret-leak concerns found.
issues: The category-distribution route depends on a compliance-tracker (VERIDIAN) endpoint (category-boq-amounts) that per PROGRESS.md is only committed to an unpushed branch in that separate repo, not deployed -- until that lands, the category-distribution charts on /dashboard/hierarchy will 502. This is honestly disclosed and degrades gracefully client-side (CategoryDistributionCharts.tsx shows a friendly error message, not a crash), so it does not block merging this projexa-side PR, but it should be tracked as a follow-up to push/deploy the compliance-tracker branch or the feature stays partially non-functional in production.

PROGRESS.md itself flags that the full existing bun test suite was not re-run end-to-end (only the new dashboard-scoped tests, 12/12 pass) and the UI was not visually verified in a browser -- worth a full CI run before/after merge as normal practice, not a reason to reject given tsc/eslint were clean and the new code is additive and well-isolated.
